documents.title: AIVA Microservices Architecture and Hybrid Viva Pipeline
documents.raw_text: Chapter 3: System Architecture and Implementation Methodology. The AIVA assessment platform implements an asynchronous service-oriented architecture built on FastAPI. FastAPI acts as the primary API Gateway, ingesting incoming HTTP and WebSocket connections from browser clients. To guarantee portable deployment across cloud environments, the entire backend service is containerized using Docker. Docker containers are orchestrated across a cluster using Kubernetes pods. Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) dynamically provisions replica pods when CPU utilization exceeds 75%, maintaining sub-50ms API response latency under load. User authentication is managed via JSON Web Tokens (JWT), verifying cryptographically signed session tokens on every request. Student vocal responses are streamed in real time via WebSockets to a speech-to-text pipeline. The primary transcription service interfaces Google Speech Recognition API. To guarantee fault tolerance, the client implements browser MediaRecorder fallback. All examination session states, turn transcripts, and student performance metrics are persisted in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL employs composite B-Tree indexes on (student_id, session_id, created_at), guaranteeing logarithmic O(log N) query execution time. The academic viva examiner relies on a hybrid retrieval system. Dissertation documents are parsed and segmented into chunks. Sparse lexical search is executed using BM25Okapi with a custom technical tokenizer. Dense semantic search is executed using Gemini 2.5 embeddings with cosine similarity in ChromaDB. The ranked candidate lists from both retrieval engines are merged using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF with constant k=60). To tailor viva challenge dynamically, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning agent controls question difficulty transitions. The DQN observes student performance history and selects discrete difficulty shifts. Following viva completion, an XGBoost ensemble classifier analyzes question difficulty, student response length, and concept coverage to categorize domain-specific student weaknesses.

documents.title: Real-Time Object Detection and Spatial Feature Extraction on Edge TPUs
documents.raw_text: Object detection architectures rely on a hierarchical cascade of spatial operations. At the foundational layer, 2D Convolution applies sliding spatial kernels across image channels to compute localized dot products. The outputs of these operations form spatial Feature Maps that encode localized activations such as edges and textures. To introduce translation invariance and reduce spatial dimensions, Pooling layers (specifically Max Pooling) downsample feature activations without altering channel depth. These stacked operations compose the backbone Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). In real-time detection frameworks like YOLO, the network outputs dense bounding box predictions across anchor grids. Dense predictions frequently generate redundant, overlapping bounding boxes for a single ground-truth object. Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) is applied as a post-processing algorithm to prune duplicate candidate boxes based on pairwise Intersection over Union (IoU) scores, keeping only the highest-scoring detection.

documents.title: Hybrid Information Retrieval and Dense Vector Search for Enterprise Knowledge Bases
documents.raw_text: Enterprise question answering demands high-precision retrieval across heterogeneous documents. Inverted Index data structures store a mapping from unique words to posting lists containing document IDs and frequencies. BM25Okapi applies probabilistic term matching over inverted indexes, scoring documents using term frequency saturation and inverse document frequency penalization. However, lexical keyword matching suffers from vocabulary mismatch and synonym blindness. To address this, Dense Vector Embeddings project passages into continuous latent vector spaces using pre-trained Transformer encoders. Semantic similarity between queries and document vectors is computed via Cosine Similarity, indexed inside ChromaDB using Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs. Because sparse and dense retrievers exhibit orthogonal error modes, their ranked result lists are combined using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Finally, the combined top-k candidates are re-scored by a Cross-Encoder reranker that performs full bidirectional cross-attention across concatenated query-passage pairs.

documents.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Question Difficulty Transitions
documents.raw_text: Adaptive educational testing formalizes examiner decision-making as a sequential optimization problem. The interaction is modeled as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) defined by a tuple of states, actions, transition probabilities, and scalar reward signals. The state vector encodes student performance history and concept coverage, while actions denote discrete difficulty shifts. The Bellman Equation expresses the optimal state-value function recursively as the immediate reward plus the discounted expected future return. Q-Learning estimates action-values iteratively using temporal difference errors without requiring a model of transition dynamics. In continuous or high-dimensional state spaces, tabular Q-learning fails due to the curse of dimensionality. The Deep Q-Network (DQN) overcomes this by parameterizing the Q-function using a deep neural network. To stabilize training and prevent divergent policy oscillation, DQN introduces an Experience Replay buffer that breaks temporal correlations across consecutive state transitions, and a separate Target Network whose weights are periodically frozen to provide stable temporal difference regression targets.

canonical_concepts.description: Mathematical framework for modeling decision making where outcomes are partly random and partly under control.

documents.title: Cloud-Native Container Orchestration and Autoscaling Infrastructure
documents.raw_text: Scalable web applications require infrastructure capable of handling dynamic traffic surges. Applications are first packaged into lightweight, immutable Docker containers that encapsulate application code and OS runtimes. Kubernetes orchestrates these containerized workloads across node pools. The Kubernetes Pod serves as the smallest deployable compute unit enclosing one or more co-located containers. Incoming external traffic is routed through an API Gateway, which handles SSL termination and reverse proxy load balancing. As user load fluctuates, the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) monitors CPU and custom Prometheus metrics, dynamically adjusting the replica count of pods. Relational data is persisted in a PostgreSQL cluster. To maintain high-throughput indexing across millions of rows, PostgreSQL organizes table records with B-Tree indexes.
